intervals.label: installation begins
intervals.note: Installation of the KM3NeT research infrastructure (seafloor network and first detection units) began at this date; construction continues today as detection units are added to both ARCA and ORCA in successive sea campaigns.
intervals.quote: In the early morning of 3 December 2015, scientists and engineers started the installation of KM3NeT, which once completed, will be largest detector of neutrinos in the Northern Hemisphere.

name: KM3NeT
notes: Facility modelled as a single facility:km3net with two detector sites (ARCA off Capo Passero, Sicily and ORCA off Toulon, France), per the astro-neutrino Wave-3 brief and the KM3NeT Letter of Intent's own framing of 'a network of deep-sea neutrino telescopes'. A third site, KM3NeT-Gr (Pylos, Greece), was named in the 2016 Letter of Intent as a candidate third building-block location but is not built and is not modelled here (no sourced detector or site record); the official 'ARCA and ORCA detectors' page (2026) describes only two operating sites.
operator_ids left empty: no institution-type record for a single legal operator was created in this wave (out of scope for astro-neutrino); operator is recorded as free text only.

operator.note: No single named legal operator entity found on the official pages beyond the Collaboration itself; the KM3NeT AISBL (an international non-profit legal entity) became operational in 2026 per the organisation page, but its formal role as facility operator is not stated verbatim.
operator.quote: The KM3NeT Collaboration brings together hundreds of scientists, engineers, technicians worldwide.

summary.plain: A research infrastructure of two neutrino detectors built into the floor of the Mediterranean Sea: ARCA off the coast of Sicily, Italy, and ORCA off Toulon, France. Strings of light sensors watch for faint flashes made by neutrinos from space and from the Earth's atmosphere.
summary.technical: Deep-sea Cherenkov neutrino observatory comprising two detector arrays under construction on the Mediterranean seabed: KM3NeT/ARCA (Capo Passero, Italy, ~3500 m depth) for high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and KM3NeT/ARCA neutrino astronomy, and KM3NeT/ORCA (Toulon, France, ~2450 m depth) for atmospheric neutrino oscillations and the neutrino mass ordering. Operated by the KM3NeT Collaboration; installation began December 2015 and continues with successive sea campaigns adding detection units to both sites.
